post.title: What an IPO is, and who gets the day-one pop, with acorns
post.ig:
In 2025, US IPOs left about $13.1 billion on the table (Jay Ritter's data): the first-day gain on shares sold at the offer price, which went to the first buyers, not the companies.
An IPO is a company's first sale of shares to the public. Bankers typically keep 7% on moderate-size deals; our math: 2M shares at $20 = $40M, $37.2M after the fee.
In 2025 new stocks rose 29.3% on day one on average, but 24.4% closed below their offer price. Ritter counts 311 IPOs in 2021, 38 in 2022, 90 in 2025 (operating companies only; excludes SPACs and penny stocks, so broader trackers show more).
Insiders are usually locked up for about 180 days.
Sources: Jay Ritter, Univ. of Florida IPO Statistics (Nov 2026); Chen & Ritter (2000); Investor.gov.
